hero.title: A US virtual number for SMS verification
intro: A +1 number is the closest thing the internet has to a default: American services expect it, sign-up forms preselect it, and support flows are built around it. When a service is picky about foreign numbers, a US number is usually the one that just works.

SMS Code gives you a real American mobile number in one tap. Enter it at the verification step, and the SMS — with a code from Google, Instagram, TikTok or 100+ other services — appears in the app usually within seconds.

whyCountry.title: Why choose a US number?
body: US-based platforms treat a +1 number as home turf. Some features and sign-up paths are simply smoother with an American number — US-only app versions, services that gate registration by region, or accounts you want tied to the US market rather than your home country.

The format is familiar everywhere: +1, then a three-digit area code and a seven-digit number. Services rarely misparse it, and it draws none of the extra scrutiny that some rare country codes attract at verification time.

tips.title: Match the account region
tips.body: If you're building a US-flavored account — a US App Store profile, a US-market TikTok — use the US number together with the matching store region and app language for a consistent picture.

tips.title: Area codes don't matter
tips.body: Services validate the number, not the city behind the area code. Whatever three digits your number starts with, the verification code arrives the same way.

tips.title: If a code stalls, swap numbers
tips.body: High demand means some US numbers have seen sign-ups before, and a service may throttle them. Cancel the pending activation — the coins come back if nothing arrived — and take a fresh number.

faqs.q: Is it a real US mobile number?
faqs.a: Yes — a number on a real carrier network with a standard +1 format. Services see an ordinary American mobile number, not an internet-only shortcode receiver.

faqs.q: Which services work best with a US number?
faqs.a: US numbers are the safest default for American platforms — Google, Discord, Tinder, TikTok, Instagram — and for any service whose sign-up flow assumes a domestic number.

faqs.q: Can I use a US number from outside the United States?
faqs.a: Yes. The number lives in the SMS Code app, so your own location and SIM don't matter — you receive the code wherever you are.

faqs.q: Do I keep the number after verification?
faqs.a: The number is rented for the activation window — long enough to receive the verification code. For accounts you plan to keep, add a recovery email and app-based 2FA right after signing up.

faqs.q: What does a US verification SMS look like?
faqs.a: Like any domestic American text: the service's name or shortcode as the sender and a 4–8 digit code in the body. The full text shows in the app the moment it arrives.
